title: Chat answers from judgments
goal: The chat (quick chats and case chats) finds and cites Court of Appeal and Supreme Court judgments (2021 on, already in kb and Zilliz from court-judgments #63) as it does sections, and the law viewer lists the judgments that cite a section. Today it answers 'I search the statute corpus, not judgments' (user, 2026-11-17, seen in a headed run).
for_whom: A practising Sri Lankan lawyer who argues from judgments as much as from sections, and needs to know which recent CA/SC judgments decided a point and what they said, with the page to check.

done_check.check: One search covers laws and judgments, with an optional filter: laws only, judgments only, or one court (CA or SC). The prompt and the search tool no longer say 'statute corpus' only; asked what it searches, the chat says Sri Lankan laws and CA/SC judgments from 2021 (and a case's files).

A cited judgment reads, in the answer and on its source chip, as 'Parties, case number (date), p. N', e.g. 'Perera v. Silva, CA/WRT/0634/2023 (12.03.2024), p. 7', with N the page of the cited passage. A judgment is cited only from a passage the agent read in this chat, like a section.

Clicking a cited judgment opens it in the sidebar the same way a law opens, without the history (amended by) part: case details (court, case number, parties, date, judge), the full text with page numbers, scrolled to the cited passage and highlighted, and the court's PDF.

A section opened in the law viewer shows 'Cited by N judgments', newest first, each as Parties, case number (date). The first 10 show, then 'Show all'. A click opens that judgment at the passage that cites the section, or at its case details when only the court's listing names the section. Sections no judgment cites show nothing.
Asked for a case it does not hold (before 2021, an NLR/SLR report, a High Court case), the chat says in one line that it holds CA and SC judgments from 2021 on and never cites a case from memory.

Eval: 10 questions written in a lawyer's words from 10 judgments' subjects (the court-judgments d6 set or like it): the chat cites the right judgment for at least 7, and every judgment citation is to a passage it read. Laws-only questions in the existing eval-chat set score as before.

scenarios.steps: In a quick chat: 'What have the Court of Appeal and Supreme Court said about when a landlord can eject a tenant because he reasonably needs the house for himself or his family under the Rent Act? Give me the leading cases.'
scenarios.expect: Answers from the Rent Act section and the 2021-on judgments that decided the point, each cited as Parties, case no. (date), p. N; each chip opens the judgment at that passage; it says that older and reported cases are outside what it holds.

scenarios.steps: Open s. 4(1) of the Industrial Disputes Act from a chat's citation.
scenarios.expect: The viewer lists 'Cited by N judgments', newest first, including CA/WRT/0634/2023; clicking it opens that judgment at the passage citing s. 4(1).

scenarios.steps: Ask for a well-known 1980s Supreme Court case by name.
scenarios.expect: A one-line note that it holds CA and SC judgments from 2021 on; no case cited from memory; it offers what it does hold on the point.

scenarios.steps: In the Perera v. Silva case chat: 'Have the courts accepted non-payment of rent like ours as a ground for ejectment? Find me recent judgments.'
scenarios.expect: Cites the case's files, the Rent Act and recent judgments, each kind with its own label and viewer.

out_of_scope: Judgments before 2021, law reports (NLR, SLR), other courts: not in the corpus (court-judgments #63).
Supreme Court judgments after 2026-08-07: the live-site spider is #71.
A judgments search page or browse outside the chat and the law viewer.
Judgment history (later judgments that follow or overrule one).
OCR for the 29 scanned judgments that have only their details chunk.

decisions.note: One search tool with a filter (laws / judgments / court), not a second tool (user).
Label: Parties, case number (date), p. N (user).
'Cited by' on a law section is in this brief, newest first, 10 then Show all, opening the citing passage (user).
The judgment viewer is the law viewer without the history part (user).
A case not held: one line on what it holds, never cited from memory (user).

No court tag in the index: kind is 'judgment' for both courts; one court is a doc_key prefix match (ca:/sc:). Check the prefix filter on Zilliz first; if it fails, a court tag means a re-embed (ask the user).

s4 (Perera v. Silva case chat), two runs: /cases/bfe44a37-5c34-4bb9-a864-fde27aed98be/chats/ea37ba08-2ac8-4646-962f-116322b23c89 cited the plaint and letter of demand (4 file passages), the Rent Act s.22 and SC judgments, but 3 judgments only seen as snippets (chips 'not verified'); after the fixes /chats/6dc3a2e4-c420-427a-a19e-7311c6d89b80 cited s.22 and SC/APPEAL/88/2014, 82/2017, 92/2014, all read, but no file passage. d6: 10 judgment cases added to etl/eval_agent.json (cat judgment, gold = the judgment). Changes the eval drove, each measured: judgment searches default to weighted (question as written: gold in top 10 dense 4/10, weighted 7/10); a judgment hit carries its whole passage (`passage`, not a 300-char snippet) and counts as read in the UI and eval (unread judgment citations 13 -> 0 in every run since); judgment searches group by doc_key (10 distinct judgments per search, not ~8) and default to 20 hits (the agent's own short queries ranked the gold 12th-25th); prompt: judgments only when the question is about what the courts held, cite a judgment by its passage id (it had cited [[sc:...]] keys in 3 of 6 runs on one case: raw text in the app). Questions 5, 6, 9 were wrong, not the agent: generic points (heroin chain of custody, quit notices, the one-month rule) the agent answered from 29, 34 and 50 other judgments on the same point; rewritten with their judgment's own facts. Final (traces in the session scratchpad eval-judgment8a-c, eval-laws2): judgment 10/10, 8/10, 9/10, 0 unread judgment citations; laws 56/56 hit, 58/59 facts, the one miss a test pattern too narrow for a right answer ('I help with Sri Lankan law only'), widened. Earlier law run (before the prompt's 'judgments only for case law' line): 54/56, the Tamil case lost 6 steps to judgment searches. Cost per question: judgment ~$0.007-0.008, law ~$0.0027 (baseline $0.0017). Not done: s4's file citations vary run to run; the agent's own judgment queries are weaker than the lawyer's question (user: improve the agent later).
